messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing short-lived egress "pockets" in eu-west around 03:20 UTC. Queue depth spikes to ~12k for a few minutes, then drops; batch size drops to 1 and we get a cascade of small requests. Cost blip and some tail latency. Anyone else noticing this?
lee: I saw that too, noticed a correlated jump in outbound network egress on proxy-pool-3. Grafana panel 'eu-west / egress by cluster' shows a sharp spike.
olivia: thanks — linking the panel: https://grafana.company.internal/d/abcd1234/eu-west-egress?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now : the spike lines up with a backup job from analytics.
raj: backups?! which job? I thought the scheduled nightly was 02:00 UTC.
maria: analytics-runner v2.4 — they started a manual re-run at 03:18, per ops ticket #3142. ops-oncall: confirmed, analytics kicked an ad-hoc export to S3 (large shards). We throttled via per-namespace egress limit but looks like some batches bypassed the quota check.
lee: quick data: prometheus query I ran — sum(rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{cluster="eu-west"}[1m])) by (pod) | topk(10, sum) returned proxy-pool-3 pods as top offenders. Also noticed container_cpu_load_average spikes.
olivia: logs show repeated 429s from the egress-rate-limiter for a subset of pods, then fallback code path sending small chunked requests:
```
2026-03-17T03:19:21Z pod/proxy-pool-3-7f9f INFO egress_limiter.go:128 rate limit exceeded, fallback=chunked_upload
2026-03-17T03:19:21Z pod/proxy-pool-3-7f9f WARN uploader.go:88 chunk size=256KB, retries=3
```
raj: chunked uploads explain the batch->1 behavior. The runtime's batcher can't coalesce because sessions are split by upload handshake.
maria: cost note: rough estimate +$120 in egress for that 8-min window for eu-west. Also saw a small uptick in request error rate for customer-facing routes (p95 latency increase).
lee: two ops asks: 1) add a temporary alert to catch these short egress pockets (currently our alert looks at 5m avg and missed the 1-3m spikes), 2) correlate queue depth panel with egress so we can see alignment.
olivia: suggested alert (short window):
```
expr: increase(sum(rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{cluster="eu-west"}[15s]))[1m:15s]) > 20000000
for: 1m
annotations:
  summary: "eu-west short egress pocket"
  description: "Detect short-lived egress surges (15s windows)"
```
raj: also add a panel showing 'queue_depth by pod' next to 'egress by pod' and enable log links (Loki) from the graph for quick drilldown.
sre-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-109 egress pocket detected (manual). Assigned to ops-oncall. :rotating_light:
ops-oncall: I'll triage. Immediate mitigation: block analytics-runner svc to the external host for next 10m and pause manual exports. Also we should patch egress-quota enforcement to run earlier in the request path.
maria: long-term: consider making batcher tolerant of transient chunking — maybe a short requeue window (200ms) to allow coalescing if chunked uploads arrive rapidly. Could also add per-pod aggregate request limiting before the fallback.
lee: follow-ups: update dashboard with a 'short-pulse' alert rule, add a synthetic test that runs a small export simulation in staging to reproduce, and open a low-priority ticket to rework limiter ordering.
olivia: i pushed a grafana dashboard variant (panel layout + Loki log links) to staging — https://grafana.company.internal/d/efgh5678/egress-triage-staging
raj: for alert tuning, i'd prefer using quantiles on request_duration_bucket to avoid flapping on noisy pods. maybe alert on topk(5, increase(requests_in_queue[1m])) rather than absolute thresholds.
maria: agreed. ops-oncall can you apply the short alert and block the export for now?
ops-oncall: done — export paused and alert rule added as temporary. I'll follow up with a runbook entry for egress-pocket triage.
lee: will collect heap/profile from proxy-pool-3 pods and post in the incident thread.
maria: thanks everyone. We'll regroup after SRE postmortem if needed. :thumbsup:
